K01.rule: Join ink control groups A,B,C,D in that order. Pencil and standby values are not the signed register.

K02.rule: Keep GOOD samples in HOLD within the UTC window. For each seq 0..7 retain the greatest revision. Order by seq, pack values as unsigned 16-bit big endian, SHA256 the 16 bytes, retain the first 16 digest bytes.

K03.rule: Take the highest signed revision of CLOSED AS_LEFT records, bay order in closeout email. Join serials exactly as printed with | and no surrounding whitespace or newline. SHA256 ASCII; retain first 16 bytes.

K04.source: escrow coupon / logical printer route ESC-N
K04.rule: Resolve logical route at the incident date. Use the last ACK attempt for that exact job. XOR its 16-byte RECOVER payload with masked_component; payload bytes are opaque, not a digest or text.

K05.rule: Reject bad CRC. For each latch 0..3 choose the greatest sequence among matching node/event and UTC window. Concatenate four opaque 4-byte words in latch order. Do not reverse bytes inside a word.

K06.rule: Use the revision authorized in the email trail. Concatenate page control strips in SERVICE_ORDER; export/scanner page order is not service order.

K07.rule: Select the transfer confirmed by Gabriel's final custodian receipt. Require COMMIT with dry_run=false. Take the checkpoint for each seq 0..7 from that transfer's CHUNK records, greatest attempt per seq. Concatenate checkpoint hex as raw bytes; SHA256, first 16 bytes.

K08.source: keeper's desk phrase, crew notes and noticeboard drafts
K08.rule: Recover the keeper's caption for the spirit of the late watch, rather than the technical incident title. Lowercase it; replace characters other than ASCII a-z, digits, and whitespace with spaces; collapse whitespace and trim. HMAC-SHA256 with desk_nonce decoded as hex as the key and normalized UTF-8 phrase as the message; retain first 16 bytes. The commitment is the acceptance check, including for remembered or reconstructed wording.

combined.rule: ASCII prefix, then K01..K08 as uppercase 32-character hex strings, each followed by one LF. SHA256 the complete ASCII bytes.
